nodes.label: ISO 19144-2:2023 Land Cover Meta Language (LCML), Edition 2
nodes.author: ISO/TC 211 and UN FAO (joint International Standard)
nodes.norm_label: iso 19144-2:2023 land cover meta language (lcml), edition 2
nodes.rationale: Specifies the LCML as a UML metamodel so different Land Cover classification systems can be described on physiognomic aspects and compared/integrated without replacing them; standardizing one metalanguage avoids the need to standardize classification systems (§8.1).

nodes.label: LC_ArtificialSurfaceCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: 0 to many artificial surface characteristics may be associated with an LC_ArtificialSurfaceElement to refine it.

nodes.label: LC_ArtificialSurfaceType
nodes.rationale: Generic name of an artificial surface defined by its external appearance and generic intended use; empty at metalanguage level.

nodes.label: LC_ClassCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Optional descriptive element relating to a whole Land Cover class (combination of strata/elements), not to physiognomic structure; informative not normative.

nodes.label: LC_ClimateCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Climate description methods are user-defined; empty at metalanguage level.

nodes.label: LC_ConstructionStatusType
nodes.rationale: Values: finished, in-progress, abandoned.

nodes.label: LC_DumpSite
nodes.rationale: The detailed kind of material dumped is considered Land Use, not Land Cover.

nodes.label: LC_ElementCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Optional descriptive element applied to a single basic metalanguage-element; the same characteristic may be applied several times to one element.

nodes.label: LC_ErosionType
nodes.rationale: Values: waterErosionSheet, waterErosionRill, waterErosionGully, gravityErosion, iceErosion.

nodes.label: LC_Extraction
nodes.rationale: The detailed kind of material extracted is considered Land Use.

nodes.label: LC_ExtractionType
nodes.rationale: Values: surface / subsurface.

nodes.label: LC_GeographicalAspectsCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Describes well-known geographic types (beach, bay, estuary, shore, urban-periurban) that are not Land Cover specific.

nodes.label: LC_GeoType
nodes.rationale: Values: beach, bay, estuary, shore, urban-periurban.

nodes.label: LC_HardpanType
nodes.rationale: Values: ironpan/laterite, petrocalcic, petrogypsic.

nodes.label: LC_PermafrostCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Depth is negative to height and, being measurable over an area, is represented as a range.

nodes.label: LC_RocksSurfaceElement
nodes.rationale: A rock surface element is a geologically consolidated formation.

nodes.label: LC_UrbanPark (removed)
nodes.rationale: Removed; replaced by code list value urban-periurban in LC_GeoType.

nodes.label: Characteristic (classification)
nodes.rationale: Distinguishing qualitative attribute of a metalanguage basic element; characteristics are informative not normative so other sets can be used with the LCML basic elements.

nodes.label: Register for extension of the metalanguage
nodes.norm_label: register for extension of the metalanguage
nodes.rationale: ISO 19144-4 defines the structure of the register, not its contents; national bodies or organizations set up their own register instances so a national classification system can be perfectly described using standard elements plus registered extensions.

nodes.label: Extension through registration
nodes.rationale: Most code lists are representative or empty at the metalanguage level so that users can populate or extend them through a register rather than hard-coding values in the standard.

nodes.label: Test A.2 Conformance of a Land Cover classification system
nodes.norm_label: test a.2 conformance of a land cover classification system
nodes.rationale: Capability test: inspect the generated model by composing LC_LandCoverClassDescriptor metaclasses for each UML class of the classification system, expressed in LC_Elements, LC_LandCoverElementCharacteristics and LC_ClassCharacteristics. URI https://standards.isotc211.org/19144/-2/1/LandCoverSystem.

nodes.label: Test A.4 Extension of the Land Cover Meta Language
nodes.norm_label: test a.4 extension of the land cover meta language
nodes.rationale: Capability test: inspect classes, attributes and code lists to ensure extensions are documented so they can be registered. URI https://standards.isotc211.org/19144/-2/1/MetaLanguageExtension.

nodes.label: ISO 19144-4 Registration and implementation for LC/LU classification
nodes.norm_label: iso 19144-4 registration and implementation for lc/lu classification

nodes.label: attribute patternOccurrence
nodes.rationale: Describes the range of probability that a recurrent feature is part of the whole class, allowing heterogeneous areas (e.g. agricultural mosaic where ponds are less frequent) to be represented.

nodes.label: cover attribute (promoted to LC_Element)
nodes.rationale: Promoted with elementSpreadingGeometry and new density attribute to LC_Element so they can be expressed for any land cover element rather than only specific cases.

nodes.label: LC_HorizontalPattern
nodes.rationale: Orders LC_Stratum objects into one or more horizontal patterns for complex features perceived as a unicum independent of scale, and to detail vertical/horizontal relations of elements; all attributes optional, null when only one stratum.

nodes.label: LC_InterStrataRelationship
nodes.rationale: Association class between LC_Stratum instances with optional onTop attribute (default baseline); constraint: a stratum cannot have an interStrataRelationship with itself directly or via circular reference.

nodes.label: LC_LandCover
nodes.rationale: Composed of LC_Element objects organised into strata (LC_Stratum) and horizontal patterns (LC_HorizontalPattern); LC_LandCoverClass is the serialization of the LC_LandCover object.

nodes.label: LC_LandCoverClassDescriptor
nodes.rationale: Metalanguage-level abstraction for a single Land Cover class; the link to the ISO 19144-1 classification system structure. Composed of LC_Element occurrences organised via LC_HorizontalPattern and LC_Stratum (UML strong aggregation/composition).

nodes.label: LC_LandCoverClassificationSystemMetaLanguage
nodes.rationale: Root UML class of the LCML model; an aggregation (metaLanguageSystemCollection) of LC_LandCoverClassDescriptor objects that when serialized describe a whole classification system.

nodes.label: LC_PlanarStrataComposition
nodes.rationale: Optional relationship class on multiStrataComposition carrying strataPortioning; portion and cover are different concepts (portion sum <= 100%).

nodes.label: LC_Stratum
nodes.rationale: Grouping of LC_Elements forming a layer; constraint: sum of cover of all LC_Elements in one stratum cannot exceed 100%; strata are independent so their cover may overlap.

nodes.label: LC_StratumPresenceType (code list)
nodes.rationale: Values fixed (default), optional, conditional; conditional useful for ambiguous legend definitions or to signal further refinement is possible.

nodes.label: Cover (horizontal disposition attribute)
nodes.rationale: Area of incidence of an LCML basic element over the substratum within its area of pertinence; expresses horizontal disposition of an LC_Element.

nodes.label: Element portioning
nodes.rationale: Percent of area of pertinence for each basic element when two or more share a stratum; sum over the stratum must equal 100%. Distinct from strata portioning.

nodes.label: European Union Common Agricultural Policy (pro-rata grasslands)
nodes.norm_label: european union common agricultural policy (pro-rata grasslands)

nodes.label: Horizontal pattern
nodes.rationale: Mechanism to describe a complex Land Cover object composed of two or more distinct Land Cover features treated together as a unicum independent of scale (e.g. tiger bush, polders, dehesas).

nodes.label: JRC tegon concept
nodes.rationale: The LC_HorizontalPattern structure is based on the tegon concept developed by the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission, used in the EU Common Agricultural Policy.

nodes.label: Land Cover
nodes.rationale: Defined as the observed (bio)physical cover on the Earth's surface (source: UN FAO LCCS 2005); treated as a geographically explicit feature other disciplines (Land Use, climate, ecology) can use as reference. Determined at one moment; distinct from land use.

nodes.label: Layering / canopy effect
nodes.rationale: Strata are used only when a layering effect exists; without it, elements compete for the same space in one stratum.

nodes.label: <<metalanguage>> stereotype
nodes.rationale: Applied to a class whose instances are other classes; a particular type of interface at a higher level of instantiation so that Land Cover classification system elements conform to the metalanguage interface.

nodes.label: Two or more elements in the same stratum
nodes.norm_label: two or more elements in the same stratum

nodes.label: Strata portioning
nodes.rationale: Percent portion by which a stratum forms part of the whole (sum of related strata projected in orthogonal plane = 100%); allows expressing situations where elements obscured by others (e.g. beneath tree canopy in satellite imagery) cannot be seen.

nodes.label: Stratum (layer)
nodes.rationale: The structural object used to describe vertical disposition; several vegetated or abiotic elements combine into a layer, and any number of strata combine into a descriptor object. No limit on number of strata or elements.

nodes.label: Tegon (3-dimensional elementary biophysical feature, JRC)
nodes.rationale: Developed by the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission and applied in EU Common Agricultural Policy use cases; an agro-forestry class is treated as an intrinsic mix of tegons having different numbers of strata.

nodes.label: Unicum (heterogeneous set treated as one unit)
nodes.norm_label: unicum (heterogeneous set treated as one unit)

nodes.label: Vertical and horizontal characterization of Land Cover (Annex F)
nodes.norm_label: vertical and horizontal characterization of land cover (annex f)
nodes.rationale: Annex F added to define the rules/syntax and boundaries of the interrelated LCML items cover, partition, strata and horizontal pattern, since the same semantics can be expressed in different ways.

nodes.label: Vertical pattern / inter-strata relationship
nodes.rationale: Vertical relations such as 'grass under trees' are expressed by composing strata with an interStrataRelationship (onTop); important for agricultural crop monitoring.

nodes.label: Arnold et al. 2016 The EAGLE Concept
nodes.norm_label: arnold et al. 2016 the eagle concept

nodes.label: Land cover classification system design criteria
nodes.norm_label: land cover classification system design criteria
nodes.rationale: Because metalanguage objects are heterogeneous, all vegetated classes derive from one physiognomic-structural approach combining growth-form elements with properties arranged in strata; non-vegetated metaclasses use the same physiognomic approach based on surface material; characteristics can be added at any level.

nodes.label: LC_CoarseMineralFragmentType
nodes.rationale: Values: gravel, stone, boulder, mixed.

nodes.label: LC_DuneType
nodes.rationale: Values: barchan, parabolic, longitudinal.

nodes.label: LC_ElementHorizontalArrangement
nodes.rationale: Optional component of LC_Element carrying cover, density (with densityUnitOfMeasure) and elementHorizontalSpreading; keeps LC_Element purely physiognomic while adding horizontal structure information.

nodes.label: LC_MacropatternType
nodes.rationale: Values gilgai and termiteMounds were included because they are the most common macropattern features in many parts of the world (Africa, South America).

nodes.label: LC_OtherArtificialSurface
nodes.rationale: Optional attribute sealed indicates whether the surface is porous and allows absorption of surface water.

nodes.label: LC_PermittedRealValue (Real, positive or negative; negative = depth, positive = height)
nodes.norm_label: lc_permittedrealvalue (real, positive or negative; negative = depth, positive = height)

nodes.label: LC_SoilSandDepositsSurfaceElement
nodes.rationale: Covers unconsolidated sediment natural surfaces.

nodes.label: LC_TopographicalAspectsCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Attributes altitude, slope (absence = unknown; 0 = flat) and slopeExposition.

nodes.label: LC_InorganicDepositType
nodes.rationale: Values: salt, soda, lime, gypsum.

nodes.label: LC_OrganicDepositType
nodes.rationale: Values: ombrothrophicPeat (rain/snow fed), minerothrophicPeat (mineral-carrying water fed); peat types may be further described by LC_PeatType.

nodes.label: UNESCO 1973 International Classification and Mapping of Vegetation
nodes.norm_label: unesco 1973 international classification and mapping of vegetation

nodes.label: C Douglas O'Brien
nodes.contributor: leadership in land cover / land use classification and sustained contributions to the ISO 19144 series

nodes.label: John Latham
nodes.contributor: project lead of the ISO 19144 series

nodes.label: Conformance class 1: Description of a Land Cover classification system
nodes.norm_label: conformance class 1: description of a land cover classification system
nodes.rationale: Requirement 1: a description of Legends or Application Schema shall be a set of UML classes with attributes corresponding to instantiations of Clause 8 metalanguage classes or Clause 9 extensions.

nodes.label: Conformance class 2: Comparison of Land Cover classification systems
nodes.norm_label: conformance class 2: comparison of land cover classification systems
nodes.rationale: Requirement 2: comparison is performed by describing each system per Requirement 1 then identifying class-by-class differences; level of detail depends on use case.

nodes.label: Feature (GFM feature type)
nodes.rationale: At the Application Schema level, classes of a classification system correspond to features in the ISO 19109 general feature model.

nodes.label: Sustainable Development Goals / global reporting frameworks
nodes.norm_label: sustainable development goals / global reporting frameworks

nodes.label: Levels of abstraction (metalanguage, classification system, application schema, data)
nodes.norm_label: levels of abstraction (metalanguage, classification system, application schema, data)
nodes.rationale: Multiple levels exist to solve interoperability problems arising from different feature definitions in different Application Schemas and classification systems; decomposition of a semantic concept into constituent elements is a common technique to establish an ontology, so classes with shared elements can be compared even when class names differ.

nodes.label: Land Parcel Identification System (LPIS) of Portugal
nodes.norm_label: land parcel identification system (lpis) of portugal

nodes.label: Test A.3 Conformance of a comparison process of two classification systems
nodes.norm_label: test a.3 conformance of a comparison process of two classification systems
nodes.rationale: Capability test: generate a model for each system, identify classes that are identical, generalizations/specializations, or similar based on shared LCML descriptor elements, and generate a mapping. URI https://standards.isotc211.org/19144/-2/1/LC_Comparison.

nodes.label: XML encoding of Application Schema (ISO 19118 / ISO/TS 19139-1)
nodes.norm_label: xml encoding of application schema (iso 19118 / iso/ts 19139-1)
nodes.rationale: XML is considered a neutral default encoding derivable from a UML Application Schema; an XML schema is implemented for the Application Schema, not for the LCML metalanguage.

nodes.label: ISO 19123 series Coverage geometry and functions
nodes.norm_label: iso 19123 series coverage geometry and functions

nodes.label: UN FAO Land Cover Classification System (LCCS v3)
nodes.norm_label: un fao land cover classification system (lccs v3)
nodes.rationale: LCML is derived from the concepts of UN FAO LCCS version 3, but deliberately drops fixed value ranges, specific classifier definitions and detailed rules to increase international acceptability; LCCS is one parametric system compliant with the LCML metamodel.

nodes.label: Di Gregorio & Jansen 1997 Africover Land Cover Classification
nodes.norm_label: di gregorio & jansen 1997 africover land cover classification

nodes.label: UN FAO 2000 LCCS v1 user manual
nodes.norm_label: un fao 2000 lccs v1 user manual

nodes.label: UN FAO / Southampton / STIIMA-CNR 2022 Land Characterization Meta-Language
nodes.norm_label: un fao / southampton / stiima-cnr 2022 land characterization meta-language

nodes.label: SIOSE Spain land occupation information system
nodes.norm_label: siose spain land occupation information system

nodes.label: UN FAO 2022 World Reference Base for Soil Resources
nodes.norm_label: un fao 2022 world reference base for soil resources

nodes.label: Anderson et al. 1976 USGS land use/land cover classification
nodes.norm_label: anderson et al. 1976 usgs land use/land cover classification

nodes.label: Sandra Branteback
nodes.contributor: Chair of ISO TC211; signed the Foreword

nodes.label: Matieu Henry
nodes.contributor: Convenor of ISO TC211 Advisory Group 13 on land cover and land use

nodes.label: Lifeng Li
nodes.contributor: Director, Land and Water Division (NSL), FAO; signed the Foreword

nodes.label: Fatima Mushtaq
nodes.contributor: Land Cover Monitoring Specialist at FAO; facilitated publication process

nodes.label: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
nodes.norm_label: food and agriculture organization of the united nations (fao)
nodes.rationale: FAO and ISO partnered since 2003 to standardize land cover and land use approaches; ISO permits FAO to republish the ISO 19144 series to ensure equitable access for Member Nations.

nodes.label: ISO/TC 211 Advisory Group 13 on land cover and land use
nodes.norm_label: iso/tc 211 advisory group 13 on land cover and land use

nodes.label: Feature catalogue (ISO 19110)
nodes.rationale: The Legend of classes corresponds to a feature catalogue; the set of feature classes can be established as a feature catalogue in conformance with ISO 19110.

nodes.label: LC_ / EL_ / LM_ prefix convention
nodes.rationale: ISO/TC 211 convention: UML class names carry a three-letter prefix identifying the standard and package; LC_ for this document, EL_ for examples, LM_ for the Annex B meta model, CL_ for ISO 19144-1, CV for ISO 19123-1.

nodes.label: Legend (nomenclature)
nodes.rationale: A Legend is concrete and established for a specific geographic area; a classification system is one semantic level above it and the LCML another level above that.

nodes.label: LC_FloristicAspectsCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Species name derived from a single plant or the dominant/most frequent species in a group; scientific names preferred.

nodes.label: LC_GroupOfPlantSpeciesType
nodes.rationale: Values: statisticallyDerivedPlantGroup / nonStatisticallyDerivedPlantGroup.

nodes.label: LC_NameAttributionCriteriaCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes whether a floristic name is derived from a single plant species or from a group of plant species.

nodes.label: LC_SinglePlantSpeciesType
nodes.rationale: Values: dominant / mostFrequent.

nodes.label: LC_SpeciesName
nodes.rationale: Empty at metalanguage level; may be populated by registration or treated as a character string.

nodes.label: Discrete coverage
nodes.rationale: A classification system's result is represented as a discrete coverage (ISO 19144-1) whose geometry may be polygons, point clouds, curves, grids or TINs; the LCML addresses element meaning, not geometry.

nodes.label: ISO 19123-1 Schema for coverage geometry and functions
nodes.norm_label: iso 19123-1 schema for coverage geometry and functions

nodes.label: LC_ConstructionMaterial
nodes.rationale: List of hardness states for construction materials; empty at metalanguage level.

nodes.label: LC_GrazedCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Addresses only the physiognomic appearance of grazed land (intensity as a percentage from light to heavy); the Land Use activity of grazing is described in ISO/TS 19144-3.

nodes.label: LC_LinearSurface
nodes.rationale: Linear surfaces (roads, railways, power line corridors) are named for physiognomic appearance only; a 'railway' in Land Cover does not imply transport use, which belongs to ISO/TS 19144-3.

nodes.label: LC_LinearSurfaceType
nodes.rationale: Empty at metalanguage level; restricted to purely physiognomic aspects.

nodes.label: LC_MowedCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Addresses only the physiognomic appearance of mowed land; the Land Use activity of mowing is in ISO/TS 19144-3.

nodes.label: LC_PloughedCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Addresses only the physiognomic appearance of ploughed land; the Land Use activity of plowing is in ISO/TS 19144-3.

nodes.label: Backward compatibility through registration
nodes.rationale: Because a primary purpose of the LCML is comparison between classification systems, vocabulary changes must be controlled and backward compatible: no metalanguage object may be deleted; objects are extended with attributes or replaced by new subobjects while the old object stays as deprecated.

nodes.label: Clause 9 Extension of LCML
nodes.rationale: Details on registration were removed from Clause 9 and replaced by an external reference; Clause 9 now explains only how extension operates.

nodes.label: Deprecated registered item
nodes.rationale: When a code list is extended the old version is superseded by a new object; the old list remains in the register with its old identifier and date, and the relationship between new and deprecated item classes must be described so the comparative aspect of the language still works.

nodes.label: Test A.5 Backward compatibility of the Land Cover Meta Language
nodes.norm_label: test a.5 backward compatibility of the land cover meta language
nodes.rationale: Capability test: extensions to classes must be by subtyping or new independent classes, and attribute/code-list extensions must not change the meaning of existing elements. URI https://standards.isotc211.org/19144/-2/1/MetaLanguageBackwardCompatibility.

nodes.label: Division of ISO 19144-2:2012 into three parts
nodes.norm_label: division of iso 19144-2:2012 into three parts
nodes.rationale: Registration material moved to ISO 19144-4 and land-use material to ISO/TS 19144-3 to separate land cover physiognomy from land use activities and registration procedure.

nodes.label: LC_ForbsLeafType
nodes.rationale: Empty at metalanguage level; populated through registration.

nodes.label: LC_ForbsStatus
nodes.rationale: Values: rooted / non_rooted.

nodes.label: Annex C.18 Example 17 Wooded peatland (spruce mire)
nodes.norm_label: annex c.18 example 17 wooded peatland (spruce mire)
nodes.rationale: Modelled by strata composition alone because tree spread is uniform (not clustered) and a canopy effect exists over the grass/moss layer; onTop=PreviousE1 links vegetation to the organic layer beneath.

nodes.label: IPCC 2003 Good Practice Guidance for LULUCF
nodes.norm_label: ipcc 2003 good practice guidance for lulucf

nodes.label: Kuechler & Zonneveld 1988 Handbook of Vegetation Science
nodes.norm_label: kuechler & zonneveld 1988 handbook of vegetation science

nodes.label: Maarit et al. 2014 Ecological restoration in drained peatlands, Finland
nodes.norm_label: maarit et al. 2014 ecological restoration in drained peatlands, finland

nodes.label: Strasburger et al. 1991 Lehrbuch der Botanik
nodes.norm_label: strasburger et al. 1991 lehrbuch der botanik

nodes.label: Cowardin et al. 1979 Classification of Wetlands
nodes.norm_label: cowardin et al. 1979 classification of wetlands

nodes.label: Milenov et al. 2022 Semantic assessment of land cover types (JRC128087)
nodes.norm_label: milenov et al. 2022 semantic assessment of land cover types (jrc128087)

nodes.label: LC_AllometricMeasurementsCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Attributes trunkDiameter and crownDiameter.

nodes.label: LC_BurntStatusCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Percentage of plants affected by fire to the extent they can no longer regenerate.

nodes.label: LC_CropGrowingParameterCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Attributes seedingTime and growingLength (uom default months, January = month 1) plus overlapGrowing percentage.

nodes.label: LC_CropYieldCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: No default uom for yield, so the uom attribute of LC_PermittedPosRealRange must be used.

nodes.label: LC_DeadStatusCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Percentage of a growth form which has died.

nodes.label: LC_EvenAgeCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: E.g. an afforestation where trees are planted at the same time, distinct from a forest following a full natural cycle.

nodes.label: LC_FieldSizeCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Not the geometric shape of the instance but the size of individual fields or plots, an indication of the type of agriculture (few industrial farms vs many small market-garden plots).

nodes.label: LC_IrrigationType
nodes.rationale: Values: surface, sprinkler, drip.

nodes.label: LC_MechanicalErosionControlFeatureCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Human erosion-control activity (terracing, contour ploughing) produces a physiognomic modification of the land that is a Land Cover feature.

nodes.label: LC_MechanicalErosionControlFeatureType
nodes.rationale: Values: contourPloughing, terracing, windBreak.

nodes.label: LC_OrchardAndOtherPlantationCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Plantation producing an output such as a crop while the plants remain.

nodes.label: LC_OverlapGrowingToReferenceCropCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Describes intercropping: a second crop begins to grow during the growth period of the first (e.g. beans intercropped with chick peas in Rwanda and Burundi), in addition to the sequentialTemporalRelationship.

nodes.label: LC_TreePlantationCharacteristic (LC_ForestPlantationCharacteristic)
nodes.rationale: Plantation whose purpose is to produce trees (timber, firewood); plants are cyclically harvested. Only the biophysical physiognomic aspect is addressed.

nodes.label: LC_UnevenAgeCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Percentage of each group of plants having the same age; useful for forest inventory.

nodes.label: LC_WaterStressCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Percentage of plants that are water stressed.

nodes.label: LC_WaterSupplyPeriodCharacteristic
nodes.rationale: Attributes rainfedPercentage, postfloodingPercentage, irrigationPercentage and irrigationType describe the crop water supply.

nodes.label: interStrataRelationship (onTop / temporal association)
nodes.rationale: The association is navigable in only one direction and is 1 to 0..1, so the UML association class can be implemented as an attribute on the instantiated object, which is how the examples show it.

nodes.label: LC_Building
nodes.rationale: A building may be non-rectangular and cover only part of the element area; percentage cover is given by the cover attribute of LC_ElementHorizontalArrangement.

nodes.label: Coarse fragments (abiotic surface element: stones, boulders)
nodes.norm_label: coarse fragments (abiotic surface element: stones, boulders)

nodes.label: LC_LeafAspectType
nodes.rationale: Values: sclerophyllous (leather-like), succulent (fleshy), soft-leaved (common state).

nodes.label: LC_LeafCharacterSize
nodes.rationale: Leaf size ranges: large > 400 cm2, medium 4-400 cm2, small < 4 cm2.

nodes.label: Example C.10 Bare field planted with wheat same year (temporal)
nodes.norm_label: example c.10 bare field planted with wheat same year (temporal)

nodes.label: Example C.8 Boreal and hemi-boreal forest (four strata)
nodes.norm_label: example c.8 boreal and hemi-boreal forest (four strata)
nodes.rationale: No height, cover or leaf attribution is given intentionally so the class remains very general.

nodes.label: Example C.5 Boulders with moss in a grassland (onTop)
nodes.norm_label: example c.5 boulders with moss in a grassland (ontop)
nodes.rationale: Two strata are used specifically so the onTop relationship can be shown; the example illustrates the relationship, not different approaches to modelling Legends.

nodes.label: Example C.7 Building with roof garden (complex onTop)
nodes.norm_label: example c.7 building with roof garden (complex ontop)

nodes.label: Example C.13 CORINE class 111 Continuous urban areas
nodes.norm_label: example c.13 corine class 111 continuous urban areas

nodes.label: Example C.14 CORINE class 244 Agro-forestry areas
nodes.norm_label: example c.14 corine class 244 agro-forestry areas
nodes.rationale: Tree cover is not given in the CORINE description and was interpreted as 5-30 %; in LCML the user can avoid specifying the Cover property.

nodes.label: Example C.12 CORINE class 311 Broad-leaved forests
nodes.norm_label: example c.12 corine class 311 broad-leaved forests
nodes.rationale: Tree layer (Natural or Seminatural) with cover 30-100 % and broad-leaved 75-100 % is Fixed; shrub layer is Optional; representation refers to the specific textual definition, not later CORINE refinements.

nodes.label: Example C.16 Herbaceous with sparse tree/shrub (Global Map)
nodes.norm_label: example c.16 herbaceous with sparse tree/shrub (global map)

nodes.label: Example C.4 Grassland with patches of coarse fragments (two elements, one stratum)
nodes.norm_label: example c.4 grassland with patches of coarse fragments (two elements, one stratum)

nodes.label: Example C.6 Mangrove swamp (mixed elements in two strata)
nodes.norm_label: example c.6 mangrove swamp (mixed elements in two strata)
nodes.rationale: Combining a vegetation layer and a water layer expresses 'flooded or regularly flooded vegetation' without complex definitions.

nodes.label: Example C.17 Montado complex agricultural Land Cover (LPIS Portugal)
nodes.norm_label: example c.17 montado complex agricultural land cover (lpis portugal)
nodes.rationale: Grass with trees and grass without trees are treated as separate physical features (tegons) with different strata, because vegetation beneath trees is subject to different agronomic practices and is accounted separately for effective grazed area; their mix is managed via LC_HorizontalPattern.

nodes.label: Example C.3 Tree and shrub savannah in three strata
nodes.norm_label: example c.3 tree and shrub savannah in three strata

nodes.label: Example C.2 Tiger bush (horizontal pattern)
nodes.rationale: One Land Cover type with two horizontal patterns (elongated shrub patches 15-25 %, open grassland 75-85 %); default attribute values (presenceType=Fixed, onTop=Baseline) are omitted from diagrams because absence implies the default.

nodes.label: Land Use
nodes.rationale: Arrangements, activities and inputs people undertake in a land cover type; multiple land uses can coexist at one location whereas land cover classes are mutually exclusive. Addressed in ISO/TS 19144-3, not this document.

nodes.label: LC_FloatingIceType
nodes.rationale: Values: lakeIce, riverIce, seaIce, fastSeaIce, driftSeaIce.

nodes.label: LC_IceType (empty code list, populated by registration)
nodes.norm_label: lc_icetype (empty code list, populated by registration)

nodes.label: LC_PeriodicVariation
nodes.rationale: Attributes periodType, persistencePeriod (>0), persistenceUnits (TimeMeasure, required iff persistencePeriod exists) and description (only if a period type is chosen) describe how a water/ice surface varies over time.

nodes.label: LC_PeriodicVariationType
nodes.rationale: Values: atmospheric, daily, tidal, seasonal.

nodes.label: LC_SnowType
nodes.rationale: Values: powder, crud, crust, slush.

nodes.label: LC_TerrestrialIceType
nodes.rationale: Values: iceCaps, iceFields, glacier, rockGlacier, tidewaterGlacier.

nodes.label: LC_WaterAndIceDynamics
nodes.rationale: Values: flowing / standing.

nodes.label: LC_WaterBody
nodes.rationale: Depth is negative to height.

nodes.label: LC_WaterBodyPositions
nodes.rationale: Values: aboveSurface / belowSurface.

nodes.label: LC_AlgaeStatus (code list)
nodes.rationale: Values floating and submerged; extensible by registration.

nodes.label: LC_Element
nodes.rationale: Abstract generalization of all basic elements; 'pure' single-concept; with no subtype it describes an area with no data. Definitions of subtypes are in the Annex D glossary as reference (non-prescriptive) definitions.

nodes.label: LC_ElementHorizontalSpreadingType (code list)
nodes.rationale: Values: unevenlySpread, regularRowsGeneral, regularRowsSingleElement, regularMultipleSingleElement, clusters, other; extensible by registration.

nodes.label: LC_ElementPresenceType (code list)
nodes.rationale: Values fixed (default), exclusive (XOR), conditionalTemporal, precluded; enables modelling crop rotations, fallow cycles and explicit absence.

nodes.label: LC_ElementRelationInSameStratum
nodes.rationale: Optional association class between LC_Elements in the same stratum with attributes temporalType and lengthOfTemporalRelationship; enables optional (conditional) and exclusive (XOR) elements and sequential temporal crops.

nodes.label: LC_LifeFormSpecializationType (code list)
nodes.rationale: Values bamboos, climbers (lianas), epiphytes, stem succulents, tuft plants; bamboos are taxonomically grasses but placed with woody growth forms because they are woody.

nodes.label: LC_OnTopType (code list)
nodes.rationale: Nine predefined values (baseline default, previousE1, previousE2, previousE3, previousE1-2, previousAll, stratum1E1, stratum1All, stratum2E1, stratum2All); a code list is used so any number of values with explicit meaning can be defined; more complex relations (previousE4, stratum3E4) left to registration for simplicity and rarity of use.

nodes.label: LC_SequentialTemporalRelationshipType (code list)
nodes.rationale: Values sequentialSameYear (length in months) and sequentialOtherYear (length in years).

nodes.label: relationship sequentialTemporalRelationship
nodes.rationale: Constraint: an LC_Element can have a sequentialTemporalRelationship only with the next one in the ordered list of elements in the same LC_Stratum.

nodes.label: Basic metalanguage-element
nodes.rationale: Elements constituting the main physiognomic aspects of biotic and abiotic cover features (trees, shrubs, herbaceous vegetation); further defined by metalanguage-element properties.

nodes.label: Annex D Glossary of Land Cover meta-elements
nodes.norm_label: annex d glossary of land cover meta-elements
nodes.rationale: Comparison via LCML requires agreement on terms; the glossary is one reference set, and differing glossaries require ontological mapping (semantic interoperability) which is out of scope.

nodes.label: Physiognomy
nodes.rationale: General appearance of an object or terrain without reference to underlying scientific characteristics; LCML bases class definition on physiognomic/structural aspects to keep the metalanguage independent of any particular classification system's semantics.

nodes.label: Semantic interoperability / ontology bridging of glossaries
nodes.norm_label: semantic interoperability / ontology bridging of glossaries

nodes.label: Extension by registration
nodes.rationale: Code lists are left empty or extensible so they can be populated via an ISO 19144-4 register; if not registered, a code list reference is treated as a character string. This keeps the LCML open-ended and extensible.

nodes.label: General rules for classification
nodes.rationale: Two governing factors: the physiognomic appearance of basic meta-elements (LC_Vegetation, LC_AbioticSurface) and the layering/strata of vegetated and abiotic elements.

nodes.label: Antonio Di Gregorio
nodes.contributor: pioneering work conceptualizing and developing LCML (ISO 19144-2) and LUML (ISO 19144-3)

nodes.label: UnitOfMeasure (ISO 19103 interface, default Metric MKS)
nodes.rationale: The optional uom attribute (constraint uomDefault) is only used when the unit of measure differs from the default Metric MKS per the International System of Units; uom is an interface to uomIdentifier, a CharacterString.

nodes.label: Class (classification)
nodes.rationale: Term 'class' conflicts between UML sense and classification sense; adjectives ('UML class', 'classification class', 'legend class') are used to reduce confusion.

nodes.label: Extension process of the LCML
nodes.rationale: The fixed vocabulary (subtypes of LC_Element) may only be changed by amendment of the document so that extension is well controlled by the standardization process and descriptions remain comparable.

nodes.label: Land Cover Meta Language (LCML)
nodes.rationale: A logical general model describing land cover feature characteristics used as classifiers plus the rules constituting a classification system. Built as a UML metamodel so that any Land Cover classification system (CORINE, Africover, Anderson, Global Map, national) can be described and compared without being replaced; it is not itself a nomenclature or set of classes.

nodes.label: Land Use Meta Language (LUML)
nodes.rationale: LUML (ISO 19144-3) can be used alone to describe Land Use or combined with LCML to describe classification systems mixing Land Cover and Land Use aspects.

nodes.label: UML instance diagrams (EL_ prefix convention)
nodes.rationale: Annex C examples are UML instance diagrams (not class diagrams); instance object names begin with EL to distinguish them from other instance objects in the ISO/TC 211 harmonized model and avoid name clashes with other International Standards.

nodes.label: Metalanguage attributes as templates
nodes.rationale: Any attribute in a metalanguage-level class is an attribute descriptor, a template for use at a lower level of instantiation; value objects define allowable numeric types with constraints but take no values at the metalanguage level.

nodes.label: LCML basic principle
nodes.rationale: A Land Cover class is described by a metalanguage object formed from a unique combination of pure independent metalanguage-elements; attributes at metalanguage level are templates for attributes one or two instantiation levels below.

nodes.label: Pure (single concept) element principle
nodes.rationale: Each metalanguage object represents a single independent concept, so two classes from different systems can be compared by the list of elements combined to describe them (A+B+Q vs A+B+Y differ by Q).

nodes.label: Wetland definition variability across jurisdictions
nodes.rationale: Existing systems are set in law in some nations and definitions such as wetland vary by jurisdiction, so the LCML must be flexible enough to describe and compare rather than replace them.

nodes.label: LC_Deciduous
nodes.rationale: Attributes starting and length capture when new leaves appear (January = month 1) and how long they persist; uom defaults to months.

nodes.label: LC_GrowthFrequency
nodes.rationale: Values: annual, biennial, other.

nodes.label: Percentage sum constraint (<= 100 %)
nodes.rationale: Percentage in leaf type / phenology links pertains to the percentage of the element in the coverage, not the property in the element; sums per growth form must not exceed 100 %.

nodes.label: Annex D (thresholds and detailed code list values)
nodes.norm_label: annex d (thresholds and detailed code list values)
